content.comment_body: Hello, everyone. I'm facing an unusual issue when trying to connect to the [product_name] web server (using [product_name] [version_no]). I access the web server through a generated link from the RemoteManagementSystem of a Teltonika RUT240 cellular router. For example: [url] When I click the link, the [product_name] web server start page appears. However, when I enter the password (4 digits), I receive a message: "Log on fail: 706" at [url]. This same message appears even if I use an incorrect password. I'm not sure where the issue is arising. Any suggestions? Help would be greatly appreciated.
Are you connecting over your home network or through the internet?

I'm connecting via the internet. If I plug a LAN cable directly into the [product_name], I can log in to the web server using local access (IP 192.168.1.7). I can share the generated link and password for the PLC if needed (it’s not currently connected to any systems).

Has anyone found a solution for this? I'm encountering the identical issue when trying to connect remotely using [company_name] [product_name] [version_no] with Teltonika RMS remote access. The web server login page appears, but "Log on fail: 706" occurs for both valid and invalid login attempts. However, local LAN access lets me log in to the web server without problems.

analysis.insight_summary: Multiple users are experiencing a login error ('Log on fail: 706') when accessing the web server of [product_name] [version_no] remotely via a Teltonika router's Remote Management System, while local access functions smoothly. The login page displays but refuses entry regardless of the credentials provided. This points to an issue specific to remote access, which may be caused by network routing, remote authentication handling, or security settings on the web server.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to securely authenticate and access the [product_name] [version_no] web server both locally and through the Teltonika Remote Management System, without encountering authentication problems.
